children.content:
# 🐙 Git Internals, Plumbing & Advanced Workflows Track

Welcome to the **Git Internals, Plumbing & Advanced Workflows Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth curriculum covering Git content-addressable object databases (Blobs, Trees, Commits, Tags), plumbing vs porcelain commands, interactive history rewriting (`rebase -i`), reflog disaster recovery, worktrees, bisect automated debugging, and repository maintenance.

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-object-database` | Content-Addressable Storage | `.git/objects`, SHA hash addresses, 4 core object types, `git cat-file` |
| `01-plumbing-vs-porcelain-commands` | Plumbing & Low-Level Git | `hash-object`, `mktree`, `write-tree`, `commit-tree`, building commits manually |
| `02-staging-area-and-index-file` | Index & Staging Mechanics | `.git/index` binary format, patch staging (`git add -p`), `git diff --cached` |
| `03-branching-and-symbolic-refs` | References & HEAD | `.git/refs/heads/`, `.git/HEAD`, detached HEAD, lightweight vs annotated tags |
| `04-merging-strategies-fast-forward-and-recursive` | Merge Engines & Strategies | Fast-Forward, 3-Way Merge (ort engine), Merge Commits, conflict resolution |
| `05-interactive-rebase-and-history-rewriting` | Interactive Rebase | `git rebase -i` (pick, reword, squash, fixup, drop), linear commit history |
| `06-git-reset-soft-mixed-hard` | Reset Modes Decoded | `git reset --soft` vs `--mixed` vs `--hard`, staging area & tree states |
| `07-git-revert-and-safe-undo` | Safe Undoing with Revert | Public branch safety, `git revert -m 1` for merge commits, audit trail |
| `08-reflog-and-data-recovery` | Reflog & Disaster Recovery | `.git/logs/HEAD`, recovering deleted branches, `git fsck --lost-found` |
| `09-git-cherry-pick-and-patching` | Cherry-Pick & Patches | `git cherry-pick -x`, `git format-patch`, `git apply`, backporting fixes |
| `10-git-stash-and-worktrees` | Stash & Multiple Worktrees | `git stash push -u`, `git worktree add` (multi-branch simultaneous checkout) |
| `11-git-bisect-binary-search-debugging` | Automated Bug Hunting | `git bisect start/good/bad`, automated script execution (`git bisect run`) |
| `12-git-hooks-client-and-server` | Git Hooks Automation | `.git/hooks/`, `pre-commit`, `commit-msg` linting, Husky integration |
| `13-submodules-and-subtrees` | Submodules & Subtrees | `git submodule add/update`, `git subtree` monorepo component management |
| `14-git-lfs-and-large-files` | Git Large File Storage | Git LFS pointer files, `.gitattributes`, tracking large binaries & models |
| `15-git-attributes-and-ignore` | Attributes & `.gitignore` | Line endings (`text eol=lf`), custom diff filters, merge drivers, ignore rules |
| `16-distributed-workflows-and-remotes` | Remotes & Upstream | Remote tracking branches, `git pull --rebase`, forks, SSH key security |
| `17-repository-maintenance-and-packfiles` | Packfiles & Garbage Collection | `.git/objects/pack`, delta compression, `git gc --prune=now`, repo sizing |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 Git Internals gotchas + Reflog Branch Resurrection Master Drill |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `example.sh` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.sh` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.sh` — Complete reference solution.

# 00 — Git Content-Addressable Storage

## 🎯 The 4 Core Object Types
1. **Blob**: Raw binary file data (does NOT store filename or permissions!).
2. **Tree**: Directory listing mapping names and mode bits to blob/tree SHA hashes.
3. **Commit**: Points to root Tree, parent commit SHA(s), author, and commit message.
4. **Annotated Tag**: GPG-signed reference pointing to a specific commit.

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 00: Inspecting Git Object Types ==="
echo "git cat-file -t <SHA>  # Prints object type"
echo "git cat-file -p <SHA>  # Pretty prints content"

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "hello world" | git hash-object --stdin

# 01 — Git Plumbing vs Porcelain Commands

## 🎯 Plumbing Commands
- `git hash-object -w file.txt`: Creates Blob in `.git/objects/`.
- `git write-tree`: Captures staged Index as a Tree object.
- `git commit-tree <tree_sha> -m "msg"`: Creates Commit object directly!

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 01: Low-Level Object Construction ==="
BLOB_SHA=$(echo "Content created by Trak" | git hash-object -w --stdin 2>/dev/null || echo "hash-calculated")
echo "Created Blob SHA: $BLOB_SHA"

# 03 — Branches & Symbolic References

## 🎯 What is a Branch?
A branch is literally a **41-byte text file** in `.git/refs/heads/<branch>` containing a 40-character commit SHA + newline!

children.name: example.sh
starter.sh
solution.sh

# 04 — Merge Strategies: Fast-Forward vs 3-Way

## 🎯 Fast-Forward
If no new commits exist on target branch, Git simply advances the branch pointer forward.

echo "Command: git merge --no-ff feature-branch"

# 05 — Interactive Rebase (`git rebase -i`)

## 🎯 Golden Rule of Rebasing
**Never rebase commits that have been pushed to a shared public branch.**

# 06 — Reset Modes: `--soft`, `--mixed`, `--hard`

| Mode | Moves HEAD | Updates Index (Staging) | Modifies Working Directory |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `--soft` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `--mixed` (default) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| `--hard` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Destructive!) |

starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "Command: git reset --mixed HEAD (or git restore --staged .)"

# 07 — Safe Undoing with `git revert`

## 🎯 Reverting Merge Commits
`git revert -m 1 <merge_commit_sha>` specifies which parent number to retain as mainline.

solution.sh

# 08 — The Git Reflog & Disaster Recovery

## 🎯 What is the Reflog?
Reflog tracks every single movement of the `HEAD` pointer locally, even after accidental `git reset --hard` or deleted branches!

solution.sh

# 10 — Multiple Working Trees (`git worktree`)

## 🎯 Why Worktrees?
Allows checking out multiple branches into separate directories simultaneously without stashing or context switching!
```bash
git worktree add ../hotfix-branch hotfix
```

# 11 — Automated Binary Search with `git bisect`

## 🎯 Bisect Workflow
Finds the exact commit that introduced a bug in O(log N) steps.
```bash
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v1.0.0
git bisect run npm test
```

children.content:
# 12 — Git Hooks Architecture

## 🎯 Client Hooks
- `pre-commit`: Runs linters/formatters before commit object is created.
- `commit-msg`: Validates conventional commit format (`feat:`, `fix:`).

children.name: example.sh
starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/pre-commit.sample
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if git diff --cached | grep -E "console.log|debugger"; then
  echo "❌ Error: Found debug statements in staged diff!"
  exit 1
fi
EOF
echo "✔ Sample hook generated!"
rm -f /tmp/pre-commit.sample

# 13 — Git Submodules vs Subtrees

## 🎯 Submodule Invariant
Parent repo records only the **commit SHA** of the submodule, not its file tree.

## 🎯 Pointer Files
Git LFS replaces large binary blobs with small text pointers containing the SHA256 checksum and file size.

## 🎯 Normalization
Enforces consistent LF line endings across Windows, Linux, and macOS:
```text

*.png binary
```

# 16 — Remotes & Pull Request Workflows

## 🎯 `git pull --rebase`
Rebases your local commits on top of newly fetched upstream commits, preventing messy non-linear merge bubbles.

# 17 — Garbage Collection & Packfiles

## 🎯 Delta Compression
Git packs loose object files into compressed `.pack` files with binary delta encoding, reducing repo size by up to 90%.

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 18 — High-Yield Git Internals Interview Drills

## 🧠 Top 10 Gotchas
1. **Blob Immutability**: Blobs only contain file content; moving or renaming a file produces zero new blob objects.
2. **Dangling Commits**: `git reset --hard` does not delete commits immediately; they remain reachable via `reflog` for 30-90 days.
3. **Detached HEAD Commit Loss**: Commits created in detached HEAD become unreachable when switching branches unless tagged or branched.
4. **Merge vs Rebase**: Merge preserves chronological history; Rebase produces a clean linear history.
5. **Fast-Forward Rejection**: Pushing a rebased branch requires `--force-with-lease` (safer than `--force`).
6. **Index File Role**: Staging area is a binary cache mapping paths to object SHAs.
7. **`git revert` vs `git reset`**: Revert creates a new forward commit (safe for public branches); Reset rewinds history.
8. **Three-Way Merge Base**: Git locates the Least Common Ancestor (LCA) commit to compute diffs.
9. **Submodule Disconnect**: Cloning a repo does not automatically fetch submodule contents without `--recurse-submodules`.
10. **Line Ending Corruption**: Committing CRLF into Linux repositories breaks shell scripts.

echo "1. SHA Content-Addressable Objects"
echo "2. Interactive Rebase history hygiene"
echo "3. Reflog disaster recovery"
echo "4. Multiple Git Worktrees"
echo "🚀 You have completed the comprehensive Git Mastery Track!"

git rev-list --objects --all 2>/dev/null | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' 2>/dev/null | grep '^blob' | sort -k3 -n -r | head -n 3 || echo "Command simulated."
